newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - MAY 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - MAY 26.

text.p: MLADA FRONTA DNES - Talks this weekend about the new cabinet led to the decision of Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik (ODS), Interior Minister Jan Ruml (ODS) and Industry and Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy (ODA) to step down. Kocarnik should be replaced by his advisor, Jiri Weigl. Ruml should be replaced by Petr Necas.

- The fund AGB 2 is suing Investicni a Postovni Banka because of two transactions with shares of Agrobanka and Kreditni Banka between 1995 and 1996. AGB 2 is requesting 1.25 billion crowns, according to Czech Television.

- Ceska Sporitelna will follow suit and react to the developments on the foreign exchange market by increasing its interest rates. Its base rate will increase to 14.60 from 12.60 percent. Interest on one-month deposits will increase to 16 percent, two-month to between 10 and 12.60 percent. Other rates will increase from June 1.

- The new auditor of Ceskoslovenske Plavby Labske, Coopers & Lybrand, recommended this company to create correction items and reserves for 705 million crowns, changing its profits from 25 million crowns to losses of 680 million.
- More than 30,000 people hit the Prague city streets to participate in the third annual Prague Marathon yesterday.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Intervention from the central bank on Friday brought the crown up to near the revaluation band. Some experts are still calling for an extension of the fluctuation band. President Vaclav Havel said foreign speculation is putting unwanted pressure on the crown. The central bank will stay with its current interest policy for now.
- Contracts for approximately one billion crowns were closed during the EMBAX-PRINT, INTRAMA and MDK trade fairs at the end of last week.
- Parliament approved an antidumping law, which prevents imports of goods for dumping prices.

- From summer, monthly concessionary payments for the public television station Ceska Televize (CT) will increase to 75 crowns from 50 crowns and payments for the public radio station Cesky Rozhlas will increase to 37 crowns. CT will keep its revenue from advertising.
- Two domestic transport-construction companies, ILBAU Liberec and ILBAU-SIBE in Beroun, will be merged, according to a decision from their common majority shareholder, Austrian Bau Holding.

PRAVO - During a visit to Skoda Plzen a.s., Vietnamese Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet supported Skoda's activity in his country. Skoda signed a contract last Wednesday with the Vietnamese concern Transico for a joint venture for manufacturing city buses.

- From today, Agrobanka will increase its base credit rate to 10 percent from six, and rates on revolving and one-way timed deposits from 13 to 16 percent. Its prime rate will increase from 10.5 to 14.5 percent.
- There was a year-on-year increase of money supply (M2) in the central bank in March of 7.3 percent, after subtracting demosits of SPT Telecom. Including SPT Telecom, the increase was 6.3 percent.
LIDOVE NOVINY - Defence Minister Miloslav Vyborny dismissed his deputy Jiri Payne yesterday.

- The Czech-American company ETA, which CKD Holding has represented in the United States since last year, won a public tender to manufacture underground and electric armaments for replicas of the historic streetcars in New Orleans, a contract worth $1.5 million.
- Shareholders of Komercni Banka will have a general meeting today, in which they should vote for a new general director.
- Travel agencies said fluctuation of the crown will not affect travel prices of tickets already bought and those listed in catalogues.
